edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.population: adults with obesity or type 2 diabetes
edges.mechanism: Better glycemic control, lower intraglomerular pressure, and reduced inflammatory signaling can all ease kidney stress, so any renal benefit would be expected to accrue through both hemodynamic and metabolic pathways.
edges.summary: The strongest piece here is the 2026 Corcoran systematic review in Mol Cell Neurosci, which ties glp-1 receptor agonists to kidney function in a direction that later studies largely support. That makes this edge more about calibrating magnitude and context than arguing over whether the signal exists at all.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
